findings.F1: The coin's standardised 3-day return predicts the return of the hour that starts at 12:00 UTC (about 16,974 non-overlapping cases), with a slope of -10.7 bp per standard deviation (t -11.4), the strongest of all 24 hours. The slope is negative in all six coins (BTC -3.3 bp t -2.2, ETH -7.6 t -4.0, LTC -10.9 t -4.5, XMR -18.6 t -8.3, XRP -9.5 t -3.7, ZEC -14.4 t -5.0) and in six of eight years (2021 -25.1 bp t -8.7, 2022 -19.9 t -7.4). This is a clock hour with no funding settlement, which matches the brief's own failure condition.
findings.F2: Hourly moves reverse. Sorting each past 1-hour return by the coin's 24-hour volatility, the bottom decile is followed by +4.6 bp excess next hour (t 7.1, n 41,310) and the top deciles by -1.6 to -3.2 bp (t -2.6 to -6.5). The slope is negative in every year from 2018 to 2025 (t -0.7 to -7.5) and in LTC, XMR, XRP and ZEC (t -5.0 to -7.8), but not in BTC (t -1.1) or ETH (t 0.1).
findings.F3: The book loses on fees, not on its forecast. Its gross gain is -0.05 bp per bar (t -1.7) against 0.71 bp of fees per bar. Its active pre-settlement bars stamped 21:00 and 22:00 lose -3.1 bp and -1.8 bp, while those stamped 13:00 earn +2.9 bp.
findings.F4: The hours stamped 20:00 and 21:00 UTC carry a positive excess drift of +4.8 bp (t 6.0) and +3.7 bp (t 4.8). It is positive in all six coins (+3.7 to +4.8 bp, t 2.5 to 3.9) and in seven of eight years. The book is short exactly into this drift before the 00:00 settlement.
findings.F5: Volume does not rise before the funding settlements. Log volume relative to its 7-day mean is -0.19 at 08:00 and -0.39 at 05:00, against its peak of +0.39 to +0.45 at 14:00 to 16:00 UTC. The volume clock follows the US session, not the funding times.
findings.F6: The 12-hour past return, scaled by volatility, predicts the next 12 hours (non-overlapping, about 5,700 cases per coin) with the same sign in BTC (t 2.7), ETH (t 3.0) and XRP (t 4.8). XMR shows the opposite sign (t -2.5). Given how many angles were checked, this is too mixed to count as a firm finding.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 3-day return, the lower its return over the 1 hour following 12:00 UTC: a stronger 3-day rise is followed by a larger decline in that hour, and a stronger 3-day fall by a larger rebound.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade the coin's 3-day trend over the hour starting at 12:00 UTC, with a position sized to the size of that trend, rather than around the funding times.
ideas.name: midday fade of 3-day trend

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's last 1-hour return relative to its 24-hour volatility, the more its return over the next 1 hour runs the opposite way.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take a short-lived position against an unusually large hourly move, larger as the move is larger relative to recent volatility.
ideas.name: hourly move reversal by volatility
